# Configuration and Persistence

Production CLI tools must remember user preferences, cache authentication tokens, load default options, and support layered configuration precedence.

## The Configuration Precedence Hierarchy

An idiomatic command-line tool resolves configuration values in a strict order of descending priority:

```text
1. CLI Flags & Options (highest priority, e.g. --timeout 30)
2. Environment Variables (e.g. MYCLI_TIMEOUT=30)
3. Local Project Config (.mycli.toml in current working directory)
4. User Global Config (~/.config/mycli/config.toml)
5. Built-in Application Defaults (lowest priority)
```

## Standard Directory Paths with `dirs`

Different operating systems adhere to different path conventions:
- Linux: `~/.config/mycli` (XDG Base Directory standard)
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/mycli`
- Windows: `%APPDATA%\mycli`

The `dirs` crate discovers these paths safely across all platforms:

```toml
[dependencies]
dirs = "5.0"
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
toml = "0.8"
```

```rust
use std::path::PathBuf;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::fs;
use anyhow::{Context, Result};

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug)]
pub struct AppConfig {
    pub api_endpoint: String,
    pub timeout_seconds: u64,
    pub verbose: bool,
}

impl Default for AppConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            api_endpoint: "https://api.example.com".to_string(),
            timeout_seconds: 30,
            verbose: false,
        }
    }
}

pub fn get_config_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    dirs::config_dir().map(|p| p.join("mycli").join("config.toml"))
}

pub fn load_or_create_config() -> Result<AppConfig> {
    let path = match get_config_path() {
        Some(p) => p,
        None => return Ok(AppConfig::default()),
    };

    if !path.exists() {
        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
            fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
        }
        let default_config = AppConfig::default();
        let toml_str = toml::to_string_pretty(&default_config)?;
        fs::write(&path, toml_str)?;
        return Ok(default_config);
    }

    let content = fs::read_to_string(&path)
        .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read {}", path.display()))?;
    let config: AppConfig = toml::from_str(&content)?;
    Ok(config)
}
```
